title: JavaScript
summary: The 20% of JavaScript that real jobs use 80% of the time: arrays and objects, async code, the DOM, professional tools, and closures and the event loop.

skip.item: The internals of prototypes and call/apply/bind
React class components, and starting with Redux

modules.title: Everyday fundamentals
learn: const and let, basic types, template literals
===, truthy and falsy values, if and the ternary operator
for...of loops
Arrow functions vs regular functions, default parameters
Block scope and closures: a function that remembers variables from where it was created

build.title: Solve 15–20 Exercism exercises; write makeCounter()
checklist: Solve 15–20 exercises on the Exercism JavaScript track

modules.title: Arrays and objects
learn: map, filter, reduce, find, some/every, includes
sort changes the original array; prefer toSorted()
Destructuring, spread/rest, ?. and ??, Object.entries
JSON.parse and JSON.stringify
Updating data without changing the original: {...obj, x: 1} and [...arr, item]. This is exactly how React state works.

build.title: Data functions on the jsonplaceholder /todos data
checklist: Save the jsonplaceholder /todos data, then write functions for completion rate per user, grouping by user, title search and top N

notNow: Generators, Symbols, Proxy, WeakMap; prototype and call/apply/bind deep dives

modules.title: The DOM and events
learn: querySelector, createElement, classList, dataset
textContent vs innerHTML: putting user input into innerHTML opens you to XSS attacks
addEventListener and preventDefault
Bubbling and event delegation
FormData and localStorage

build.title: First 10 JavaScript30 projects; to-do app
checklist: To-do app: add, edit, delete, toggle and filter, saved in localStorage. Keep one array as the source of truth and redraw the list from it (the same idea React uses).

modules.title: Async JavaScript and APIs
learn: The event loop as a concept
Promises, async/await and fetch
fetch does not throw an error on a 404, so always check response.ok
try/catch/finally and Promise.all
Loading, error and empty states in the UI
Debouncing: wait until the user stops typing before acting

build.title: GitHub profile finder
checklist: GitHub profile finder: search that waits until you stop typing, loading and 404 states, repositories sorted by stars, the user and their repositories fetched in parallel

notNow: XMLHttpRequest, callback-pyramid tutorials, writing your own Promise class

modules.title: Professional tools
learn: ES modules, npm scripts and Vite
Git: branches, pull requests and resolving conflicts
The DevTools debugger: breakpoints and the Network tab
ESLint and Prettier
Classes, plus enough about this to know that arrow functions don’t get their own this

build.title: Vite + modules; push to GitHub and deploy
checklist: Move the Week 4 app into a Vite project split into modules
Push it to GitHub with clean commits and deploy it on Netlify or Vercel

topics.title: Scope and closures
topics.why: Interviewers ask about closures more than almost anything else; learn them at the level of “I can explain it.”

topics.title: Working with arrays and objects
topics.why: Most day-to-day JavaScript work is reshaping data from an API into what the screen needs: map/filter/reduce, destructuring and spread.

topics.title: The DOM and events
topics.why: React later takes over most of this, so learn the model, not every API.

topics.title: Async code
topics.why: Promises, async/await, fetch and error handling sit behind every API call.

topics.title: The event loop
topics.why: One of the topics interviewers ask about most; explain the call stack, microtasks and tasks.

topics.title: Professional tools
topics.why: Modules, npm, Git, DevTools and Vite are how every JavaScript project is built and shipped.

topics.title: this and classes
topics.why: How a function is called decides what this is, a favourite interview question.

interviewChecklist: The event loop: call stack, microtasks and tasks
this: how the way a function is called decides it
Promises and async/await, including error handling
map, filter and reduce, written from memory

notes.title: Where to go next
items: After Week 5, JavaScript continues in the React, TypeScript and Node.js tracks: React, then TypeScript and testing, then Node.js and a REST API.

capstone.title: ApplyTrack
capstone.summary: A full-stack job application tracker built with React, TypeScript, Node/Express and a real database.
